assetRequirements.purpose: Reusable bedroom background with clear visual landmarks for Room, navigation, placement, and hotspot checks.
Reusable transparent button sprite for Interactable placement, activation, and hotspot alignment checks.
Reusable baseline Character art used to exercise ordinary Dialogue stage presentation.
Reusable smiling Character variant that makes an authored expression change visually obvious.
Reusable notification sound for exercising a causal Dialogue sound-effect cue.
Reusable spoken voice line for exercising the Dialogue voice playback path.

Minimal independently animated overlay for two Character Profiles. Reuse the small transparent button as a deliberately synthetic badge; transform/visibility frames distinguish blink, speaking and Gesture without additional sprite art.

scenarios.title: Rooms & Interactions
scenarios.description: A reusable bedroom scene proving rejected navigation, normal Interactable/Feature interaction, state mutation, successful navigation, a Fade transition, and destination lifecycle behavior.

checks.title: Initial Room and world state
checks.action: Inspect the bedroom, door, and wall button.
checks.expected: The bedroom is current, the wall button is present and enabled, and the door begins locked.

checks.title: Locked exit rejects navigation
checks.action: Click the bedroom door while it is locked.
checks.expected: The door remains hoverable and clickable, navigation is rejected, the bedroom remains current, and the locked-door notification appears.

checks.title: Interaction mutates authored state
checks.action: Press the wall button.
checks.expected: The Interaction handles the command, sets gate-unlocked true, and emits the button notification.

checks.title: Unlocked exit navigates
checks.action: Click the bedroom door again.
checks.expected: Navigation succeeds and the destination Room becomes current.

checks.title: Non-Cut Room transition
checks.action: Watch the transition after the door opens.
checks.expected: The destination is presented through a skippable 300 ms Fade rather than an immediate Cut.

checks.title: Destination lifecycle executes
checks.action: Read the arrival notification.
checks.expected: The destination after-enter lifecycle emits its arrival notification after the Room becomes current.

checks.title: Attempted navigation and directed relocation use different guard policy
checks.action: Use the guarded policy door, then activate the Directed relocation control.
checks.guideSubtext: The door attempt stays in the workshop; the directed relocation commits to the same guarded target.
checks.expected: Ordinary navigation is vetoed by the target can-enter guard and runs rejection handling. Directed Room Change reaches the target, runs normal lifecycle, and records the guard only as a diagnostic policy condition.

scenarios.title: Room Lifecycle
scenarios.description: A compact round-trip station covering source/exit/target rejection, ordered lifecycle programs and hooks, transition context, child flow, and authored transition selection.

checks.title: Source, exit, and target rejection paths stay distinct
checks.action: Try Reject at source, Reject selected exit, and Reject at target in order.
checks.expected: Each attempt remains in the source Room and emits only the rejection handling associated with the failing phase.

checks.title: Lifecycle programs run before matching hooks
checks.action: Take Successful round trip and inspect the ordered lifecycle notifications.
checks.guideSubtext: Pre-commit programs set marker Variables; matching hooks report those markers as true.
checks.expected: Before-leave and before-enter hooks observe the immediately preceding program mutations, then after-leave and after-enter program/hook notifications occur after commit.

checks.title: Room entry context reports cause and sequence
checks.action: Complete a successful entry, then use the self-loop on the destination.
checks.expected: The after-enter hook reports navigation-attempt as the cause and a monotonically advancing entry sequence; self-entry creates a new occurrence rather than reusing the prior sequence.

checks.title: After-enter can run and resume a child flow
checks.action: From the round-trip destination choose Enter child flow and complete the Dialogue.
checks.expected: The child Room after-enter lifecycle starts the authored Dialogue, waits for it to finish, then resumes and emits the return notification without losing the Current Room.

checks.title: Lifecycle behavior at a no-Current-Room boundary
checks.action: Exercise a Room transition whose source or destination has no Current Room.
checks.expected: Only the lifecycle half applicable to the existing Room runs; there is no fabricated source or destination lifecycle.

checks.title: Room transition settings select distinct presentation
checks.action: Compare project-default Cut, Exit-level Dissolve/Fade, and an explicit requested transition.
checks.expected: Transition precedence is explicit request, selected Exit override, then project default; skipping settles at the committed destination.

scenarios.title: World Composition
scenarios.description: A camera-framed Room with duplicated Interactable occurrences, Character/Prop composition, conditional overlays, placement Layouts, world-plane ordering, and authored/runtime environments.

checks.title: Background fit remains readable under a nontrivial camera
checks.action: Activate Cycle background fit repeatedly to compare contain, cover, stretch, and center around the backdrop landmarks.
checks.expected: Cropping, bars, stretching, and centered source-image geometry change according to the selected fit while the Room camera remains zoomed and rotated.

checks.title: Occurrences stay separate from authoritative Location
checks.action: Show a Character and an Interactable at multiple placements, then move them between Room and Unplaced while independently changing visibility/eligibility.
checks.expected: Occurrences remain presentation-only: Location stays authoritative, identities are not duplicated, and hidden/disabled subjects do not bypass eligibility.

checks.title: Placement resolution follows the documented precedence
checks.action: Move an Instance through explicit dynamic placement, authored occurrence, fallback, and explicit no-presentation cases.
checks.expected: The correct occurrence is selected at each precedence level, and an ordinary move with no valid placement rejects without moving semantic Location.

checks.title: Conditions and composition hook alter one draft
checks.action: Activate either cyan sample once, then again.
checks.expected: The conditional Prop and overlay appear when enabled, while the Room compose hook independently controls the Character occurrence from the same global state; the second activation restores the initial composition.

checks.title: World planes and authored order compose predictably
checks.action: Inspect the scrolling background Environment, Interactable/Character/Prop content, and overlay Environment; compare the cross-family overlap witness in Materials & Engine2D.
checks.expected: World Background stays behind World Content, World Overlay stays above it, and local authored order controls overlap within a plane without introducing hard Prop/Interactable tiers.

checks.title: A spatial placement may mount a Layout
checks.action: Inspect the Spatial Layout marker over the center Prop.
checks.expected: The authored world-placement-marker Layout is mounted at the Prop placement and follows the placement geometry rather than behaving like a full-screen overlay.

checks.title: Room camera views respect bounds and edge policy
checks.action: Compare translated, zoomed, and rotated default/named views under bounded contain versus overscan behavior.
checks.expected: Contain clamps framing to authored bounds while overscan does not, independently of semantic Location; named-view selection and Focus require an authored invocation path before this can be completed in the Lab.

checks.title: Authored and runtime environments have explicit lifetime
checks.action: Watch both scrolling authored Environments, activate a cyan sample twice, pause/resume, then leave the Room.
checks.expected: Owner, plane, UV motion, opacity, replacement/stop-key behavior, and gameplay versus unscaled-presentation clock policies remain distinct; Room-owned environments terminate when their owner ends.

scenarios.title: Engine2D Draw Texture & Specialization
scenarios.description: Two ordinary Interactable sprites use one custom Engine2D Material while a raw-image Prop crosses both sprites at an authored order between them. The renderer supplies each Interactable draw's sprite texture automatically; one Instance inherits the Definition parameter while the other specializes it.

checks.title: Renderer-owned draw texture is automatic
checks.action: Inspect both button sprites.
checks.guideSubtext: Both should still use the authored button image.
checks.expected: Both sprites retain the authored button image through the custom Engine2D Material even though the Material and both applications author no texture source for s_texColor.

checks.title: Definition and Instance parameter specialization
checks.action: Compare the left Definition sample with the right Instance sample.
checks.guideSubtext: The right sample should have a stronger cyan tint.
checks.expected: Both use the same Material and sprite, while the right sample has the visibly stronger cyan tint from its Instance u_strength override over the Definition value.

checks.title: WorldContent order interleaves Prop and Interactable draws
checks.action: Inspect the raw-image center Prop where it overlaps both cyan Interactable sprites.
checks.expected: The center Prop is in front of the left Interactable (orders 15 over 10) and behind the right Interactable (order 20 over 15), proving authored order interleaves draw families instead of using a hard Prop/Interactable tier.

scenarios.title: Dialogue & Presentation
scenarios.description: A compact authored Dialogue station proving normal line continuation, Character presentation changes, timed cues, audio, real choice UI, and a semantic branch consequence.

checks.title: Dialogue opens at a neutral checkpoint
checks.action: Confirm the Guide starts neutral and quiet, then continue past the ready line.
checks.guideSubtext: No presentation cue should fire before you continue.
checks.expected: The authored Dialogue opens on a neutral, cue-free ready line and requires explicit continuation before the presentation cue line begins.

checks.title: Dialogue voice cue plays after progression
checks.action: Listen when the presentation line begins.
checks.guideSubtext: The voice should start only after you leave the ready line.
checks.expected: The spoken line plays through the normal Dialogue voice path after explicit progression into the presentation line.

checks.title: Character presentation changes mid-line
checks.action: Watch the Guide during the presentation line.
checks.guideSubtext: The Guide should switch from neutral to smile partway through.
checks.expected: The Guide changes from the neutral presentation to the visibly distinct smile expression through the Dialogue cue.

checks.title: Dialogue sound-effect cue plays later
checks.action: Listen for the attention cue after the expression change.
checks.expected: The causal sound-effect cue is submitted through the normal Dialogue audio path later in the presentation line.

checks.title: Timed presentation cue fires later in reveal
checks.action: Keep watching after the expression change.
checks.guideSubtext: A brief flash should appear with the attention cue.
checks.expected: A brief skippable flash occurs at the later authored text offset without blocking normal Dialogue continuation.

checks.title: Real Dialogue choice is clickable
checks.action: When the presentation line finishes, continue to the choice and click Accept the signal.
checks.expected: The real RmlUi choice dispatches the authored Dialogue edge rather than a Lab-specific shortcut.

checks.title: Choice branch mutates authoritative state
checks.action: Choose Accept the signal and inspect the scenario state.
checks.expected: The choice edge sets presentation-accepted to true and the accepted Dialogue branch becomes active.

scenarios.title: Interview the guide
scenarios.description: Revisit a conditional transcript, unlock a disabled topic, inspect sparse presentation cues, call child Scenes, compare logging and follow completion destinations.

checks.title: Conditional transcript and stable history
checks.action: Continue the first greeting. Revisit before unlocking, then Unlock and revisit again.
checks.expected: The first greeting appears only once and interview-notes remains 1. The locked conditional line is skipped without setting interview-skipped; after unlock it appears and sets that Property to 1. Redirect returns to the same transcript, not a new invocation.

checks.title: Shown-disabled versus hidden choices
checks.action: At the first menu try the dimmed Read sealed topic, then Unlock. Later Finish into the hidden-policy conversation. Restart and Finish without unlocking to compare.
checks.expected: The first locked Read choice is visible but disabled and cannot advance. Unlock enables it. The hidden-policy optional topic is absent when locked and present when unlocked.

checks.title: Line, block and default speaker resolution
checks.action: Compare the initial Guide greeting with Inspect speakers, Stage Slots and skip cues; then read the off-screen Radio line.
checks.expected: Dialogue default Guide is used for the greeting. Block default Studio Guide overrides it for the tour, and line override Radio overrides the block. Names/colors follow the resolved Character. Only the matching speakerSync left occurrence speaks; the non-sync right and off-screen speakers do not acquire another person’s animation.

checks.title: Sparse and independent Stage Slots
checks.action: Choose Inspect speakers, Stage Slots and skip cues; continue through hide/show, smile+lean, Portrait, new Radio, clear and rebuild.
checks.expected: Hide/show retains left state; smile persists through sparse lean update. Portrait chooses close Pose; new Radio resets Character axes to stage/standing/neutral but stays left. Clear removes left; rebuild initializes defaults. Right remains unchanged throughout.

checks.title: Independent image and Character snapshot Media Slots
checks.action: Choose Inspect retained Media Slot states. Compare initial image, replacement snapshot, hide/show and clear once a Dialogue Layout realizer is available.
checks.expected: Image and Character snapshot media must be positioned by Dialogue UI independently of world actors; hide retains content and clear removes it. Current station authors the mutations but the built-in UI does not display them.
checks.statusReason: Runtime publishes media slot fields, but no built-in Media Slot image/Character-snapshot presentation exists. Complete with a normal Dialogue Layout consumer, not a world-actor surrogate.

checks.title: Ordered cues and skip barriers
checks.action: At the tour’s final line first let it reveal naturally. Restart, return to the tour and immediately skip that line.
checks.expected: Same-position smile then neutral ends neutral once. Natural reveal plays the disposable sound once; immediate skip suppresses it. The final awaited non-skippable wave is a barrier and its crossed sound is not replayed.

checks.title: Conceal and preserve child UI
checks.action: Choose Call concealed / preserved child Scenes and acknowledge each child caption.
checks.expected: Conceal removes caller text while the child owns Continue. Preserve keeps caller UI, but input still belongs to the child. Each return resumes the next exact Dialogue segment once.

checks.title: All Dialogue completion destinations
checks.action: Finish the interview, finish hidden choices, acknowledge Return and Room completion, then End the History tools.
checks.expected: Dialogue replacement enters hidden-policy once; Scene completion starts the completion tour; Return resumes the Scene at its Room-call Event; Room completion reaches Interview complete; End removes foreground Flow and keeps that Room. Handoff/ResumeDialogue is intentionally shared with scene-director/dialogue-handoff (#254), not duplicated here.

checks.title: Nested effect cursor and observable boundaries
checks.action: Unlock then Read sealed topic. Acknowledge the child caption, then read the receipt.
checks.expected: The receipt is issued and notification emitted before the child Scene. The false nested branch is skipped; after return RunLua stamps once, yielding issued / stamped. No replay duplicates the suffix.

checks.title: Admitted log entries and system append/clear
checks.action: Open Menu → History after the greeting and choices. Compare the only-choices and only-lines conversations; then Append system receipt, inspect History, Clear History and inspect again.
checks.expected: Everything keeps admitted greeting/choices with speaker/origin. OnlyChoices omits its line and any individually unlogged choice. OnlyLines omits choices and private lines. Nothing in History tools logs itself; append adds one bold system notification, clear empties the log.

scenarios.title: Dress and animate one person
scenarios.description: Two independent Character occurrences expose layered Profile/Pose/Expression/Appearance selection, automatic animation, mapped Gestures and idle clocks.

checks.title: Profiles, Poses and Expression fallback
checks.action: Continue through baseline, lean, smile and Portrait.
checks.expected: Ordered body+badge layers remain intact. Lean moves only the left base. Smile changes body art. Portrait without Pose selects close; absent Smile override uses the Profile’s default Expression composition.

checks.title: Sparse Appearance over Expression
checks.action: Compare the Hide badge and Clearing Appearance lines.
checks.expected: Appearance hides only the badge over the smiling body; clearing restores the badge while revealing unchanged underlying Expression composition.

checks.title: One shared Character, two visual occurrences
checks.action: Compare left speaker-sync and right non-sync states and read the shared-identity line.
checks.expected: Visual selection/placement axes remain independent. The studio-note Property belongs to one Studio Guide and becomes dressed; its authoritative Location remains character-studio-idles despite both Dialogue occurrences.

checks.title: Blink versus speaking precedence
checks.action: Stay on baseline and watch badges; then continue with non-speaking lines.
checks.expected: Left badge uses speaking scale pulses while matching speaker; right non-sync badge blinks on its interval. Speaking takes precedence over blink on left. Body layer remains unaffected by badge clip frames.

checks.title: Mapped Gesture completion, skip and cancellation
checks.action: Let awaited wave complete. Restart and skip the skippable wave. On Cancel gesture continue immediately before its 500 ms sound cue so the next line clears left.
checks.expected: Wave temporarily moves badge and plays its crossed cue once, then returns to desired composition. Skipped/un-crossed cues are discarded, not replayed. Clearing the target cancels its operation without modifying right.

checks.title: Reconstructible idle clocks
checks.action: Finish into Idle clocks. Compare left bob, middle sway and right pulse. Open Pause, then save/load.
checks.expected: Gameplay bob/pulse stop under pause; unscaled sway continues. After load the selected loops remain, but disposable backend phase restarts rather than resuming a saved frame.

scenarios.title: Read the illustrated notice
scenarios.description: Read styled, paged and animated text with real font faces, explicit diff emphasis, wrapped object selection and mixed Unicode scripts.

checks.title: Nested styles and real face selection
checks.action: Read the first notice line; compare nested bold/italic, underline/strike, blue, outlined, large, real versus sys synthetic faces and one-run offsets.
checks.expected: Each closing span restores its outer style. Only offset text is nudged; following text restores position. Explicit DejaVu bold/oblique use real faces while sys b/i use synthetic styling. Alpha variation is intentionally shared with text-effects/fade rather than inventing an unsupported alpha tag.

checks.title: Cluster reveal and manual/delayed paging
checks.action: Continue through manual page then delayed page; resize/enlarge text before advancing. Restart and compare immediate skip.
checks.expected: Complete é/Å clusters reveal on precomputed layout. Manual page waits for input; delayed page waits 0.6 seconds. Resize preserves current page/input boundaries and does not duplicate advancement.

checks.title: Distinct effects, waits and loops
checks.action: Observe the effect line; try skipping during its final non-skippable fade and acknowledge its wait.
checks.expected: Fade/fade-across change alpha; glow/nod/shake/tremble/pop remain distinct. Loops include authored delay/yoyo; the non-skippable effect retains its wait. Effects do not change words or duplicate Continue input.

checks.title: Wrapped semantic object selection
checks.action: Increase text scale so the long linked button phrase wraps. Hover/click the linked phrase versus plain text.
checks.expected: Only actual linked glyph/span bounds select notice-button; plain text does not select it. This is semantic subject selection, not a fake notification or a general RML button hit target.

checks.title: Explicit diff emphasis
checks.action: Read the unchanged / newly emphasized / unchanged notice.
checks.expected: Only the explicitly d-marked phrase is red/diff-emphasized; surrounding text restores normal styling. Automatic Room-description diff remains automation-only.

checks.title: Mixed-script shaping and fallback
checks.action: Read Latin combining clusters, Arabic/Hebrew with English/numbers, and CJK. Wrap, resize and enlarge text.
checks.expected: Latin clusters stay intact, RTL runs order legibly amid LTR/numbers and DejaVu supplies their glyphs; IPA Gothic supplies CJK. No tofu, corrupt wrapping or claim of color-emoji support.

scenarios.title: Operate exact objects and inventories
scenarios.description: Move exact Interactable Instances through Rooms and inventories, exercise containment and owner-qualified Features, then mutate stack quantities without losing identity semantics.

checks.title: Definition peers keep exact Instance identity
checks.action: Use Identity, then inspect Specimen A and B after A moves to Player Inventory and B becomes Unplaced.
checks.expected: Both remain distinct Instances of one Definition with their own identity-tag Property values. Room, Inventory, and Unplaced Location changes do not collapse or recreate either identity.

checks.title: Owner-qualified inventories present direct members
checks.action: Use Inventories to open the Player, Character, Interactable, Interactable Feature, and Room Feature inventories together.
checks.expected: Each view resolves the exact owner-qualified Inventory and shows only direct members; nested contents are not flattened. The current Project exercises built-in fallback presentation, while the mutually exclusive Project-default Layout branch remains blocked.
checks.statusReason: A running Project has one immutable inventory.defaultLayout setting: built-in fallback requires it to be null, while Project-default Layout resolution requires it to be non-null. The station covers all owner kinds and fallback without inventing a second project variant; complete the default/explicit/fallback matrix when Feature Lab supports per-scenario project-setting variants.

checks.title: Containment preserves direct Location and rejects cycles
checks.action: Use Containment to move the filled container to Delivery; inspect the child's direct Location and effective Room. Cycle rejection remains blocked for authored Test playback.
checks.expected: The child remains directly located in the container Inventory while its effective Room follows the moved ancestor. A containment cycle must reject atomically and leave the container in Delivery.
checks.statusReason: The station and semantic Test cover ancestor effective-Room propagation and preserved direct Inventory Location. The normal Lua move API queues a containment-cycle request, whose later atomic rejection is surfaced as an error diagnostic; authored Test playback treats any runtime error diagnostic as execution error, so it cannot currently assert that expected rejection as a passing Test without suppressing the real diagnostic.

checks.title: Enabled and visible remain independent
checks.action: Use Enabled / visible after the identity step.
checks.expected: Specimen A becomes disabled while still visible; Specimen B stays enabled while hidden in Player Inventory. Eligibility and display state do not imply one another.

checks.title: Quantity creation honors stackability and limits
checks.action: Use Create quantity to request 12 stackable supplies and quantity 2 of a non-stackable specimen.
checks.expected: Twelve supplies create the minimum three fresh stacks, each at or below limit 5 and without coalescing existing stock. Non-stackable quantity 2 creates two distinct quantity-one identities.

checks.title: Split creates identity; merge ends donor
checks.action: Use Split / merge on the four-unit Room stack.
checks.expected: Split leaves the source identity with quantity 2 and creates one quantity-2 peer inheriting Room presentation; merge restores the original receiver to 4 and ends the donor identity.

checks.title: Whole and partial exact transfers preserve the right identities
checks.action: Use Exact transfer for one whole stack and two units from another.
checks.expected: Whole transfer moves the existing identity. Partial transfer leaves the source at quantity 2 and creates exactly one quantity-2 destination identity without automatic coalescing.

checks.title: Aggregate quantity operations use stable compatible selection
checks.action: Use Aggregate on the isolated Aggregate bin.
checks.expected: Add fills compatible stacks in stable identity order, aggregate transfer splits only the boundary identity, direct totals remain exact, and consuming the exhausted source ends that identity while the surviving stock stays quantity 2.

checks.title: Invalid quantity mutations reject without partial change
checks.action: Use Rejections after Aggregate to try insufficient exact transfer and an aggregate transfer spanning incompatible stack classes.
checks.expected: Both mutations reject atomically. The exact source stays quantity 2 in its Room; aggregate pure totals can still span standard and premium classes even though an ambiguous mutating selection cannot.

checks.title: Same-named Features remain owner-qualified
checks.action: Use Feature owners to compare slot on Specimen A, Specimen B, and the Room.
checks.expected: Each same-named Feature resolves separate Properties and Inventories from its exact owner; subject identity and inventory ownership never collapse to the Feature id alone.

scenarios.title: Layer Properties and live Traits
scenarios.description: Exercise typed and schema-less Properties across exact owners, fallback precedence, runtime Trait capabilities, and recursive Conditions using effective live state.

checks.title: Typed Property values validate at runtime
checks.action: Use Typed values.
checks.expected: Boolean, integer, finite number, string, enum, and Message values resolve. Fractional integer, unknown enum, and non-finite number writes reject without replacing valid state.

checks.title: The same local key remains exact-owner scoped
checks.action: Use Owner-local.
checks.expected: shared-state changes independently on Room, Character, exact Interactable Instance, and Feature owners, including a different Character schema; Global mutation is demonstrated with global-shared-state. Exact Global/local key overlap is blocked by the runtime's project-wide Global Property namespace.
checks.statusReason: A declared Global Property ID is authoritative project-wide: identity-qualified lookup of the same key resolves it as Global and rejects the identity target. The station still exercises the same local key across Room, Character, Interactable Instance, and Feature owners plus a separate Global key; mark this ready when the runtime can represent the assigned Global/local same-key overlap.

checks.title: Override, explicit null, and unset follow fallback precedence
checks.action: Use Precedence.
checks.expected: A runtime override wins, explicit nullable null remains present, and unset reveals the next layer: Instance, Definition, Archetype, or Trait default as authored for each specimen.

checks.title: Schema-less Properties distinguish absence, null, and value
checks.action: Use Dynamic.
checks.expected: The key changes scalar type, becomes explicit null while remaining present, rejects a structural configuration that would introduce an incompatible Boolean schema, preserves prior state atomically, then returns to absence after unset.

checks.title: Live Traits add and remove capabilities without copying structure
checks.action: Use Traits to add/remove marker and Property-backed Traits and inspect the exact Instance before and after each change.
checks.expected: Trait presence and trait-value appear and disappear on the exact Instance without copying structural fields. Trait-selector dispatch and Condition evaluation must also observe runtime-added Traits.
checks.statusReason: The semantic Test covers runtime Trait add/remove and Property-backed capability resolution on the exact Instance. In aggregate authored playback, Interaction dispatch rejects a binding selected solely by that runtime-added Trait and Condition evaluation cannot reliably resolve the newly attached Trait-backed Property, so the live selector/Condition branches remain blocked until runtime authority is corrected.

checks.title: Recursive Conditions resolve mixed authoritative leaves
checks.action: Run Typed values, then use Recursive Condition.
checks.expected: All / Any / Not compose Property, Trait, exact Location, owner Inventory quantity, Lua, Current Room, and bound interaction-slot leaves; the successful rule marks conditions-hit true. Command-result lifecycle/provenance is exercised by Runtime Workshop rather than fabricated in a scope where Interaction programs do not expose sibling results.

scenarios.title: Build and mutate runtime Instances
scenarios.description: Materialize Archetypes, create compiled/effective clones, replace structural configuration, retarget a live Exit, and destroy Instances while respecting dependents.

checks.title: Archetype materialization creates independent mutable Instances
checks.action: Use Materialize.
checks.expected: Room and Character Archetypes materialize with archetype provenance. Two Character Instances keep different birth Locations, and a runtime Property written to one does not leak to its sibling.

checks.title: Runtime creation preserves source provenance and fresh identity
checks.action: Use Create / clone.
checks.expected: Rooms and Characters created from compiled/effective sources receive distinct usable IDs and compiled-definition/clone provenance; an Interactable created from its Definition starts Unplaced with a fresh identity.

checks.title: Structural configuration replacement preserves mutable world state
checks.action: Use Replace / clear.
checks.expected: Replace and clear preserve the target's Room Location and disabled state. A schema conflict and removing an Inventory with a live dependent both reject atomically; clearing returns immutable birth configuration.

checks.title: Live Exit retargeting changes ordinary Room navigation
checks.action: Use Retarget annex, then navigate through the annex Exit.
checks.expected: Ordinary Room navigation follows the live destination and arrives in Annex B. Map projection/navigation is intentionally owner-deferred for #252 and is not simulated here.

checks.title: Destruction is non-cascading and ended IDs stay ended
checks.action: Use Destroy.
checks.expected: A free Instance ends; destroying an owner with a live Inventory dependent rejects and preserves both owner and child; a later creation receives a different ID and cannot resurrect the ended identity.

scenarios.title: Discover and build named commands
scenarios.description: Exercise Primary Activate, explicit and rule-derived Offers, selector specificity and rank, discovery-versus-authority, and the built-in named-slot Command Builder.

checks.title: Primary Activate dispatches only a unique complete winner
checks.action: Activate Primary, Menu, and Ambiguous targets. Use explicit Open Verb Menu on Menu and choose an action.
checks.expected: The unique complete primary command dispatches immediately. A non-primary target requires the Verb Menu, while competing primary candidates resolve through the menu instead of guessing.

checks.title: Offer specificity, rank, and suppression are deterministic
checks.action: Activate Exact, Prefix, Trait, Definition, Feature, Rank, Rule Offer, and Suppressed targets.
checks.expected: Exact and longer qualified patterns outrank trait/definition/reusable-Feature selectors, which outrank family and any-subject. Rank breaks equal specificity. The rule-derived Offer participates normally, and a false winning Offer condition suppresses the Verb rather than falling through to a broader Offer.

checks.title: Discovery does not define command authority
checks.action: Compare the condition-suppressed target with a direct valid Probe command, then inspect Unavailable Probe while its availability is false.
checks.expected: The suppressed command is absent from discovery but the same fully bound valid Probe command still executes through semantic command submission. Verb availability remains the authority boundary and rejects Unavailable Probe while false.

checks.title: Named slots and bindingOrder drive command construction
checks.action: Start Deliver from the Recipient, bind the Parcel from Project Inventory, and submit through the built-in Command Builder. Also execute Deliver with the same parcel bound to both named slots.
checks.expected: bindingOrder requests recipient before parcel even though slot declaration order differs; execution binds by slot name, not position. Inventory subjects are selectable, and one live subject may legally occupy both compatible slots.

checks.title: Command Builder drafts rebind and cancel without persistence
checks.action: Begin Deliver, use Rebind on an already selected slot, choose another compatible subject, then Cancel. Repeat and leave the Room before submission; save/load around an incomplete draft if desired.
checks.expected: Rebind changes only the transient Layout-owned draft. Cancel or leaving the owning context discards the draft, and incomplete builder state is never part of save-persistent gameplay state.

checks.title: Contextual menus preserve trigger context and clamp to the viewport
checks.action: Open the Verb Menu from the near-edge Menu target with pointer input, then invoke the same subject action through non-pointer/Open Verb Menu input.
checks.expected: Pointer invocation anchors to the triggering point and clamps inside the viewport; non-pointer invocation uses the stable subject/default anchor. Menu choice continues to refer to the original triggering subject.

scenarios.title: Resolve Interaction rules and transaction boundaries
scenarios.description: Exercise live subject selectors, Guard containment tiers and priority, fallback stages, immediate atomicity, and observable command boundaries with deliberate failure controls.

checks.title: Interaction selectors resolve live subject identity
checks.action: Resolve the Character, Definition, Trait, Feature, and Exact controls, then use the runtime-created parcel placed on room entry.
checks.expected: Character family, exact Instance, owner-qualified reusable Feature, live Trait, and origin Definition selectors match the live subject. The runtime-created parcel retains its origin Definition for selector matching; no selector depends on Archetype ancestry.

checks.title: Containment tiers resolve before same-tier priority
checks.action: Run Guard tier before and after Enable guard.
checks.expected: A false narrow Guard falls through to the broader tier; once true, the narrower containment tier beats the broader rule regardless of priority. Same-tier priority and equal-winner ambiguity are intentionally shared with the focused native Interaction resolver tests so the canonical Lab remains free of deliberately ambiguous authoring diagnostics.

checks.title: Unhandled work falls through every authored fallback stage
checks.action: Invoke Fallback and inspect the final response. Compare with handled controls and the deliberate post-boundary failure.
checks.expected: No matching rule, an unhandled Verb default, and the explicit unhandled Project fallback advance in order to the localized engine response. Once handled work crosses an observable boundary, later failure does not restart fallback or replay prior effects.

checks.title: Immediate command groups commit atomically
checks.action: Invoke Atomic failure, which stages a marker mutation before an intentionally impossible exact quantity consume; then use Verify state.
checks.expected: The quantity rejection emits its real runtime diagnostic and the earlier staged marker mutation is rolled back, proving no partial commit within the immediate group.

checks.title: Observable boundaries commit prefixes and resume at the exact cursor
checks.action: Invoke Boundary failure, acknowledge its notification and child Flow, then let the nested branch reach its deliberate quantity failure. Use Verify state afterward.
checks.expected: The pre-notification and post-notification mutations commit around the observable notification boundary, the child Flow returns to the nested command cursor, and the later failure does not replay the notification/Flow or erase already committed effects.
